verdict_reason: 13 tiles found. 11 of the 13 are a single photographer's (71138480@N00) continuous walk-through of one complex, and two frames in that run are hard proof: 3858328114 and 3858315842 both show the Khue Van Cac - the two-tier red timber pavilion with paired circular 'moon' windows on a square rendered stone base - which exists only at the Temple of Literature. 3858312622 shows the Van Mieu Mon entrance gate (two-storey, three arched openings, inscribed plaque, clipped topiary) from the inside, and 3858326318 catches a turtle on the brick lip of the Thien Quang well, whose white balustrade panels with the circular fret motif are the same balustrade that appears in the foreground of the Khue Van Cac shot. The remaining frames from that photographer (courtyard, Dai Trung Mon, Thai Hoc courtyard seen from an upper floor, bronze bell, bronze king statue, old banyans on the brick perimeter wall) are all internally consistent with the same site and the same lighting/weather. Both singleton photographers also fit: 12452548125 is the same style of stone lantern against the same old red-brick wall that appears in 3858324862 from the other photographer. Only one frame (an indoor portrait in a carved wooden frame) cannot be tied to the place. This pin is on its real subject, not a place centroid.

photos.evidence: Carved stone lantern (den da) with a flared cap and pierced star-shaped openings, standing in clipped groundcover against a wall of old orange and blackened bricks, with a mossy flat stone slab at left. Same lantern type, same old brick wall and same low hedge as 3858324862 from a different photographer in this pile; no text visible, so the tie is fabric-matching only.

Shot from under an open red-columned, pantile-roofed gate building hung with red silk lanterns, looking through three bays onto a paved courtyard with more red-columned pantiled halls, bonsai in ceramic pots and a green ceramic incense urn on a plinth. Matches the Dai Trung Mon / Dai Bai courtyard sequence of Van Mieu, and it sits inside the same photographer's confirmed Khue Van Cac run.

Bronze seated statue of a robed, bearded mandarin in a cylindrical official's cap, holding a tablet, in front of a large plain red-lacquered panel, with a carved fan/phoenix-tail throne back behind him. Reads as one of the bronze commemorative statues in the Thai Hoc house of Van Mieu; inside the same photographer's confirmed run but no inscription legible.

Looking down from an upper storey over two sweeps of old red pantile roof onto a brick-paved courtyard containing a small open timber pavilion on a stone platform, bonsai in stone pots, and a low colonnaded wing at right. City rooftops just visible over the trees. The vantage point (an upper floor) and the bell/drum pavilion layout match the Thai Hoc courtyard at Van Mieu; same photographer, same overcast light as the confirmed frames.

Very large banyan-type tree with a fluted, root-clad trunk spilling surface roots onto mown grass, growing hard against a red brick wall with a cement coping. Same red brick wall and coping as 3858324862; a garden inside a walled compound, not a street tree.

The Van Mieu Mon entrance gate seen from the inner (first courtyard) side: two-storey whitewashed and weathered structure, three arched openings at ground level, an upper storey with three tall arches, a pierced balustrade, curved roof with dragon finials, an inscribed plaque on the upper face, flanking piers with vertical Han inscriptions, and rows of clipped ball-topiary trees in front.

The Khue Van Cac seen over a mossy rendered wall: two-tier red timber pavilion, upper storey with a large circular lattice 'moon' window on each face, pierced red balustrade, tiled roof with pale ceramic ridge figures, set among big old trees. This pavilion is unique to the Temple of Literature.

Wide brick/flagstone courtyard with lines of low stone benches down both sides, big frangipani and umbrella-shaped conifers, and a three-bay red-columned building with an old pantile roof and red lanterns closing the far side. Matches the first courtyard of Van Mieu looking at Dai Trung Mon; same photographer and same day as the confirmed Khue Van Cac frames.

Two Western visitors standing either side of a very large bronze bell with cast dragon-medallion bosses and relief panels, hanging on a timber frame over red brick paving; a carved stone lantern and a stone drum stand on the lawn behind, and a yellow rendered building with a red-tiled roof shows through the trees. The big bronze bell plus stone lantern plus stone drum grouping matches the Thai Hoc courtyard of Van Mieu.

A curtain of banyan aerial roots pouring over a small whitewashed arched shrine and a red brick wall with cement coping; a carved stone lantern and a grey stone bench stand on the paving in front. The stone lantern and old brick wall are the same as in 12452548125 (different photographer) and the wall is the same as in 3857540315.

Two turtles on the old brick lip of a green-water pond; above them a pale green balustrade panel with a dark red circular fret motif, reflected in the water. That balustrade panel is the same design as the balustrade in the immediate foreground of 3858328114 (Khue Van Cac), i.e. the edge of the Thien Quang well in the Temple of Literature.

The Khue Van Cac head-on: square rendered stone base with two carved piers and inscribed side panels, upper storey of red timber with a large circular lattice window each side, pierced red balustrade, moss-covered tiled roof with ceramic ridge dragons; an old red brick wall runs across the frame and a white balustrade with circular-fret panels (the Thien Quang well surround) crosses the foreground.

Flash portrait of a smiling woman with a backpack sitting inside a large carved and pierced dark wooden frame, indoors; a red curtain and a gilt object out of focus behind. No signage, architecture or exterior context of any kind.
